Read Chainlink reference prices
Chainlink is the valuation reference for both underlying tokens. Each feed must be within the market's maximum feed age.
Compute token amounts from liquidity
The token amounts behind one vault token are computed from the pool's liquidity math at the reference price. For Uniswap v3 positions, they are computed from the position's liquidity and range.
Check against the pool TWAP
The approved AMM TWAP is compared with the Chainlink-derived price. It is only a consistency check. It is not averaged with the Chainlink price and does not replace it.
Report value with no haircut
LPOracle reports the full value of the liquidity per vault token. It does not discount for impermanent loss, slippage or liquidation costs.
Apply the Collateral Factor separately

Borrowing limits come from the reserve's Collateral Factor, where LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor. BorrowingCapacity = LPPositionValue × LPCollateralFactor. Collateral Risk sets the borrower's interest premium. It is not a haircut.
Uniswap v2 LP tokens
Chainlink + pool liquidity math + TWAP consistency check
Supported. 1 vault-token base unit per LP-token base unit.
Uniswap v3 positions (full-range or approved range)

Uniswap v4, Curve, Balancer, Aerodrome, SushiSwap and other AMMs
Not supported. Adding any of them requires a separate review and governance approval, including approval of its pricing method.
How LPOracle values vault tokens, and what the Aave Adapter allows when price checks fail.

Avana's LPOracle prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices. Chainlink is the valuation reference, and the pool's TWAP is a second check. For concentrated positions, token amounts are computed from the position's liquidity and range at the reference price.
LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity per vault token with no haircut. How much of that value can support debt is set separately, through each reserve's Collateral Factor on the Borrow Spoke.

Valuation and borrowing limits are kept separate. The oracle reports what the position is worth. The Collateral Factor and pool risk factor account for range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.
Vault-token value depends on:
Each vault token is priced as the value of the two token amounts it represents:
VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1
q0, q1
Amounts of token0 and token1 represented by one vault token. They are computed at the reference price from the pool's liquidity math and, for Uniswap v3, the position's range.
P0, P1
Chainlink reference prices for token0 and token1.
No haircut
The result is the full value of the liquidity. Risk adjustments are applied through the Collateral Factor, not in the price.
Vault tokens have 18 decimals and are minted 1:1 with liquidity. There is no scaling factor or exchange rate, so the oracle cannot affect how many vault tokens are issued.
LP valuation is not a single spot-price read. The path from prices to borrowing capacity has these steps:
LPOracle prices only selected Uniswap v2 LP tokens and Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum mainnet. Each approved pool has its own vault token, and so does each fee tier and range where applicable.
AMM / Position Type
Oracle Source
Notes

The approved AMM TWAP is a consistency check on the Chainlink-derived price. It is not an average of the two prices and does not replace Chainlink. It detects when pool state and reference prices disagree.
Uniswap v2
The pool's TWAP over the market's configured window is compared with the price implied by Chainlink. The window length is set per market.
Uniswap v3
The position's token amounts are computed from its liquidity and range. Before they are accepted, the pool's TWAP is compared with the Chainlink-derived price.
Tolerance
Each market has an allowed price deviation. If the TWAP is outside it, the Aave Adapter blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals.
Chainlink stays the reference
When the TWAP is outside tolerance, repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price. The TWAP is never used as the valuation price.
Other AMMs
Avana defines TWAP sources only for Uniswap v2 and v3. A TWAP source for another AMM is defined in that AMM's review and approved by governance.
Allowed deviation and maximum feed age

Each market sets an allowed deviation between the TWAP and the Chainlink-derived price, and a maximum feed age. The four conditions below determine what remains available. Separately, the Guardian can freeze a market by freezing both the vault-token reserve and the GHO reserve on its Borrow Spoke.
Chainlink valid, TWAP within tolerance
Normal operation.
Chainlink valid, TWAP outside tolerance
The Aave Adapter blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.
Chainlink stale or invalid, cached price within maximum age
The last valid price is used. New borrowing and voluntary withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue.
Cached price past maximum age
Liquidations pause until the feed recovers or governance approves a backup feed. Repayment continues.

Pledge: moves a Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position into the custody of the LP Vault. The Adapter mints vault tokens 1:1 through the Collateralization Module. It supplies them through the borrower's Position Proxy and enables them as collateral.
Borrow: borrows GHO from the Avana Hub through the Borrow Spoke. The TWAP and stale-price gates apply.
Repay: available at any time unless the Adapter is paused.
Withdraw: allowed only if the account stays healthy. The Adapter burns the matching vault tokens, and the LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT with uncollected fees.
The borrower entry point for deposits, borrowing, repayment and withdrawal, acting through each borrower's Position Proxy.

The Aave Adapter is the borrower's entry point to Avana. It coordinates deposits with the LP Vault and the Collateralization Module. When a position is pledged, the Adapter mints vault tokens and supplies them through the borrower's Position Proxy as collateral. Borrowing, repayment and withdrawal also go through the Adapter.

The Aave Adapter does not set risk parameters or collateral values. Collateral Factors, health checks and liquidation eligibility come from the Borrow Spoke, LPOracle and governance-approved parameters. Related pages:
Borrow Spoke
Liquidation Framework

A dedicated Position Proxy holds each borrower's Aave position. Every borrower action (deposit, borrow, repay, withdraw) therefore passes through the Aave Adapter and Avana's controls. Partial-settlement liquidations do not go through the Aave Adapter. In partial settlement, LPVaultSwap calls the Borrow Spoke directly. In full-position settlement, the Aave Adapter withdraws and burns all vault tokens for the position so the LP Vault can release it.

The Aave Adapter enforces the TWAP and stale-price gates. If the pool TWAP is outside tolerance, it blocks new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals. If the Chainlink feed is stale or invalid, it blocks new borrowing and voluntary withdrawals. Repayment continues in both cases.

A withdrawal is allowed only if the account stays healthy afterward. The Aave Adapter then burns the matching vault tokens. The LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT together with any uncollected fees.
The Aave Adapter is upgradeable, behind a timelock that Avana Labs cannot bypass. Contract addresses are published after deployment is approved.
Borrowers can call the contracts directly, without Avana's frontend. They keep the ability to repay and make permitted withdrawals.
Only positions that pass the Risk Module's pool and limit checks can be deposited. The Aave Adapter does not decide which pools are approved.

strings: Glossary
Definitions of Avana protocol terms, including the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes, LP Vault, vault tokens, Collateral Factor, LPOracle and settlement modes.
Core Concepts
Protocol Components
Financial Terms
Risk & Security
Metrics
Disclaimers
A standard, unmodified Aave V4 Hub owned by the Aave DAO. It holds a capped GHO credit line allocated through the GHO Reserve. Only approved Avana Borrow Spokes can draw from it.
Avana Borrow Spoke

A standard Aave V4 Spoke owned by the Aave DAO. It holds collateral-only vault-token reserves for one market category. It lends GHO under each reserve's Collateral Factor, Collateral Risk and liquidation parameters.
Avana Lend Spoke
An Aave V4 Spoke that Aave governance approves separately. It adds direct lender supply to the Avana Hub and borrowing of assets other than GHO.
Hub-and-Spoke Architecture
The Aave V4 design in which liquidity sits in a Hub and collateral rules sit in Spokes. Avana uses standard Aave V4 Hub and Spoke contracts and keeps all Avana-specific logic in its own contracts.
An approved operator that calls LPVaultSwap to liquidate unhealthy accounts. At least two keeper operators run: Avana Labs and at least one independent operator.

A liquidity position in a supported AMM pool. Avana supports selected Uniswap v2 LP tokens and Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum mainnet. Uniswap v3 is limited to full-range positions and specifically approved ranges.
Depositing an LP position into the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity from the pool.
The Avana contract that holds pledged LP tokens and NFTs. It records each position's owner, market, backing and status. It releases a position only through an approved withdrawal or settlement.

A transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 record (18 decimals) that represents pledged liquidity 1:1 on an Avana Borrow Spoke. There is one vault token per approved pool, and per range where applicable. It has no owner, no secondary market and no emissions.
Position Proxy

A dedicated contract that holds each borrower's Aave position. Every deposit, borrow, repayment and withdrawal therefore passes through Avana's controls. In full-position markets it also carries settlement authority.
Collateral Factor
The share of a vault token's value that supports debt: LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor.
Pool Risk Factor
A per-market reduction applied once to the lower underlying Collateral Factor. It reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.
Borrowing Capacity
LPPositionValue × LPCollateralFactor. Capacity also depends on existing debt, exposure caps, available GHO liquidity and oracle checks.
Market Category

One of three groups of approved markets, each with its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps: Stable LP (candidate USDC/USDT), Correlated LP (candidate wstETH/WETH) and Blue-chip/stable LP (candidate WETH/USDC).
Aave's stablecoin and the only asset borrowers can borrow from Avana.
GHO Credit Line
A capped GHO allocation from the Aave DAO to the Avana Hub through the GHO Reserve. Each increase is subject to conditions and governance approval.
Borrowing Rate
BaseRate × (1 + UserRiskPremium). For example, a 50% risk premium on a 4.5% base rate gives 6.75%.
The Avana Hub GHO base rate, which is at least the Core Hub GHO base rate.
User Risk Premium

The premium added to the base rate, set from the Collateral Risk of the borrower's collateral. With several collateral reserves, it is a weighted average. Aave V4 updates it on borrow, withdrawal, collateral change and on request.
Collateral Risk
A per-reserve setting on the Borrow Spoke that determines the borrower's interest premium. It is not a haircut on collateral value.
Health Factor
Collateral value after Collateral Factors, divided by outstanding GHO debt. An account becomes liquidatable when its health factor falls below 1.
Partial Settlement

The settlement mode for Uniswap v2 and selected Aerodrome or Uniswap v3 markets. LPVaultSwap calls Aave V4's standard liquidation with a GHO flash loan. Only the liquidity needed to restore health is removed, so the borrower keeps the rest of the position.
Full-Position Settlement

The settlement mode for most AMMs that use NFTs. LPVaultSwap repays the debt with a flash loan and settles the whole position through an approved route. Any surplus after debt, fees and costs returns to the borrower.
Liquidation Bonus
Aave V4's liquidation incentive in partial-settlement markets. It funds the keeper reward, execution costs and Avana's capped liquidation fee. It does not apply in full-position settlement.

Committed loss-coverage capital that LPVaultSwap draws on within a liquidation if proceeds fall short. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts, and debt and collateral stay unchanged. It counts only once it is funded.
Avana's oracle for vault tokens. It prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices (VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1) and applies no haircut.

A consistency check against the pool's time-weighted average price. It is not averaged into the price. If the TWAP moves outside tolerance, new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.

The borrower's entry point to Avana. It coordinates deposits with the LP Vault and Collateralization Module, then mints and supplies vault tokens. Borrowing, repayment and withdrawal also go through the AaveAdapter. It enforces the TWAP and stale-price gates but does not set risk parameters or collateral values.

The only contract that performs liquidations. It takes flash loans and runs each market's settlement route. It draws from the FirstLossReserve when needed and pays keepers, Avana and borrowers. It is not a spoke and cannot draw from the Avana Hub. It is owned by an Aave DAO executor, and its operational controls are held by an Avana Labs and Aave DAO service-provider multisig.
Checks market eligibility, the pilot allowlist, position-size limits and exposure limits at the pool, underlying-token and depositor level.
Sets the vault-token amount for each position at 1:1 with its liquidity and reconciles backing. The oracle cannot affect issuance.
Immutable, versioned contracts that execute approved exits. They redeem LP tokens, remove liquidity and collect fees.
Holds market definitions, contract mappings, Avana-side limits, oracle settings, settlement routes and fee terms.
LP Collateral
The value of LP positions held in the LP Vault and represented by vault tokens on Avana Borrow Spokes.
Outstanding Debt
The amount of GHO currently borrowed against vault-token collateral.
Credit-Line Usage
The share of the Avana Hub's GHO credit line that borrowers have drawn.
Borrowing Headroom
The difference between a borrower's current debt and their borrowing capacity on a Borrow Spoke.
Backing Reconciliation
The comparison of vault-token supply with LP Vault liquidity for each market, reported by AaveAdapterLens.
Pool Approval

Only approved pools can be used as collateral. New collateral pools are published for a two-week review before listing approval. Meme-token pools and pools without enough liquidity history or reliable external pricing are excluded.
Pilot Allowlist

During the pilot, only allowlisted depositors can pledge positions. Each market has minimum and maximum position sizes, and each account has a limit on positions. Governance can remove the allowlist once pilot criteria are met.
Exposure Caps
Limits checked at the pool, underlying-token and depositor level, including a limit on the share of a pool's liquidity. Hub add and draw caps also limit flows per Borrow Spoke.
Emergency Guardian

A multisig that can pause, freeze and cancel. It cannot upgrade contracts, change parameters or move collateral. It can freeze a market by freezing both the vault-token reserve and the GHO reserve on the Borrow Spoke.
Governance Roles

The Aave DAO owns the Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes and holds pause and freeze roles over Avana's contracts. It can stop markets without Avana Labs. Avana Labs administers its own contracts within these permissions.
Upgrade Timelock
A delay on upgrades to Avana's upgradeable contracts, followed by a grace window. Avana Labs cannot bypass the delay. The Aave DAO can cancel queued upgrades.
Avana Umbrella
Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella. It is third in the loss order, after dedicated first-loss capital and revenues committed to loss coverage.

meta.description: Core concepts behind Avana: pledging LP positions, vault tokens, LPOracle valuation, Collateral Factors, GHO borrowing and settlement modes.

strings: Key Concepts
Core concepts behind Avana: pledging LP positions, vault tokens, LPOracle valuation, Collateral Factors, GHO borrowing and settlement modes.
Core Insight
Borrowing Model
Oracle & Valuation
Borrowing Capacity
Health & Liquidation
Fee Treatment

Token collateral is usually a balance of a single asset, such as ETH, BTC or a stablecoin. An LP position is a changing combination of assets. Trades alter its inventory, prices change its value, and fees accrue over time. A concentrated-liquidity position also depends on its range and may become one-sided as prices move.

Avana therefore sets risk parameters per market. Each approved pool (and range, where applicable) has its own vault token. Each market has its own pool risk factor, settlement mode, TWAP window, allowed price deviation and maximum feed age. Each of the three market categories (Stable LP, Correlated LP and Blue-chip/stable LP) has its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps.

Users pledge an approved Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity, so the position keeps earning fees. A Uniswap v3 position stops earning fees while it is out of range.
The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with the pledged liquidity. The AaveAdapter supplies them to the market's Avana Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy.
The borrower then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub. The Borrow Spoke applies vault-token risk parameters, and the Hub keeps GHO liquidity and debt accounting.

The LPOracle prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math. It derives the token amounts behind each vault token and values them at Chainlink prices: VaultTokenPrice = q0·P0 + q1·P1. For Uniswap v3, the amounts come from the position's liquidity and range at the reference price.
The oracle applies no haircut. Each reserve's Collateral Factor handles risk separately, and Collateral Risk sets the borrower's interest premium.

Chainlink is the valuation reference. The pool's TWAP is a consistency check. It is not averaged into the price and does not replace Chainlink. If the TWAP moves outside tolerance, new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.

Borrowing capacity is the position's value multiplied by the reserve's Collateral Factor: LPCollateralFactor = min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor. The pool risk factor is applied once. It reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.

Capacity also depends on existing debt, exposure caps, available GHO liquidity and oracle checks. The borrowing rate is BaseRate × (1 + UserRiskPremium). With several collateral reserves, the premium is a weighted average.
An illustrative example of how each reserve's factor is derived is in
Collateral Factors
Health factor compares collateral value, after each reserve's Collateral Factor, with outstanding GHO debt. An account becomes eligible for liquidation when its health factor falls below 1.

Only approved keepers can call LPVaultSwap. LPVaultSwap takes a GHO flash loan, repays the debt and settles the LP collateral in one transaction. Uniswap v2 and some Uniswap v3 markets use partial settlement, which removes only the liquidity needed to restore health. Markets where partial removal is not suitable use full-position settlement, which returns any surplus to the borrower.

Pledged positions stay in the pool and keep earning trading fees. A Uniswap v3 position earns fees only while it is in range. When a borrower withdraws, the LP Vault releases the LP tokens or NFT together with any uncollected fees. Withdrawal is allowed only if the account stays healthy.

meta.description: A worked liquidation example for Avana, showing partial and full-position settlement of the same position at health factor 0.98.

strings: Liquidation Examples
A worked liquidation example for Avana, showing partial and full-position settlement of the same position at health factor 0.98.
Overview
Starting Position
Partial Settlement Example
Full-Position Settlement Example
Multi-Position Account
Edge Cases
Summary

If proceeds fall short of the debt, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged. Keepers may retry with a smaller partial liquidation.
In partial settlement, Aave V4's dust rule may liquidate a small remaining position in full rather than leave an uneconomic remainder.
If the Chainlink feed is stale and the cached price is past its maximum age, liquidations pause until the feed recovers or governance approves a backup feed. Repayment continues.
An out-of-range Uniswap v3 position holds only one of its two tokens and stops earning fees while out of range, which changes the amounts recovered on removal.
These examples apply the
Liquidation Framework
The figures are illustrative and are not market parameters. GHO and USDC are assumed to be worth $1. Governance sets the liquidation bonus, target health factor and fee caps for each market.

A borrower pledges a $100,000 full-range WETH/USDC position. The borrower receives one vault-token base unit per unit of liquidity, valued at $100,000 in total. The lower Collateral Factor of the two underlying tokens is 70% and the pool risk factor is 50%, so the LP Collateral Factor is 35%.
• Borrowing capacity is 35,000 GHO.
• The interface limit at an opening health factor of 1.10 is about 31,800 GHO.
• The borrower takes 25,000 GHO, for an initial health factor of 1.40.
• The health factor reaches 1.00 when the collateral is worth about $71,400, a fall of about 29%.
• The collateral then falls to $70,000 and the health factor to 0.98, so the account is eligible for liquidation.
With a 5% liquidation bonus and a 1.05 target health factor, Aave V4's standard liquidation repays only enough debt to restore the target.
• LPVaultSwap takes a GHO flash loan and repays about 2,564 GHO of debt.
• About $2,692 of liquidity, less than 4% of the position, is removed from the pool and swapped to GHO.
• The bonus funds the keeper reward, execution costs and Avana's capped fee. Aave's built-in liquidation fee is 0 for vault-token reserves.
• The borrower keeps about $67,300 of collateral against 22,436 GHO of debt, for a health factor of 1.05.
In a full-position market, the same position is settled in full and the surplus is returned to the borrower. The Aave liquidation bonus does not apply in this mode.
• LPVaultSwap flash-borrows 25,000 GHO and repays the debt through the Position Proxy's settlement authority.
• The Aave Adapter withdraws and burns all vault tokens. The LP Vault then releases the position for settlement through an approved route.
• Settlement realizes 69,000 GHO.
• The flash loan is repaid. The keeper reward, execution costs and Avana fee total 750 GHO, within the market's maximum percentage of debt.
• The borrower receives the remaining 43,250 GHO.

A borrower can hold more than one vault-token reserve as collateral on a Borrow Spoke. Aave V4 computes one health factor for the account, but settlement still happens position by position under each market's settlement mode.
• The borrower's interest premium is the weighted average of the Collateral Risk of each reserve.
• In partial-settlement markets, Aave V4's standard liquidation sizes repayment to its target health factor.
• In full-position markets, the full debt is repaid if the position is the account's only collateral. Otherwise, repayment is sized to the approved health target.
• Exposure limits at the pool, underlying-token and depositor level cap how much one account can hold. During the pilot, a limit on positions per account also applies.

In the same scenario, partial settlement removes less than 4% of the position and leaves the borrower with a health factor of 1.05. Full-position settlement closes the position and returns 43,250 GHO to the borrower. The settlement mode is set per market.

meta.title: Liquidation Flow
meta.description: The Avana liquidation sequence: a flash loan, debt repayment, vault-token burn, LP settlement and swap to GHO in one transaction.

strings: Liquidation Flow
The Avana liquidation sequence: a flash loan, debt repayment, vault-token burn, LP settlement and swap to GHO in one transaction.
Overview
Related Docs
Runtime Sequence
Outcomes
Keeper Notes
Detect an account below health factor 1

Approved keepers monitor accounts using the health factor that Aave V4 computes from LPOracle vault-token prices and each reserve's Collateral Factor. An account is eligible for liquidation when its health factor falls below 1.
Take a GHO flash loan
The keeper calls LPVaultSwap, which takes a GHO flash loan from the GHO FlashMinter on Ethereum. LPVaultSwap is not a spoke and does not borrow from the Avana Hub.
Repay debt and take the vault tokens

In partial-settlement markets, LPVaultSwap calls Aave V4's standard liquidation on the Borrow Spoke. The standard liquidation applies the target health factor and dust rules and transfers the seized vault tokens to LPVaultSwap. In full-position markets, LPVaultSwap repays the debt through the Position Proxy's settlement authority. The Aave Adapter then withdraws all vault tokens for the position.
Burn the vault tokens and remove the liquidity

The vault tokens are burned. In partial settlement, the LP Vault removes the matching liquidity. For Uniswap v3, it removes part of the liquidity and the NFT stays in the vault. For Uniswap v2, it redeems the matching LP tokens. In full-position settlement, the LP Vault releases the NFT for settlement through an approved route.
Swap to GHO and repay the flash loan

Proceeds are converted to GHO through CoW Swap within the same transaction. The flash loan is repaid, and the keeper reward and Avana fee are paid. In full-position markets, any surplus goes to the borrower. If proceeds fall short, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts.
Before liquidation
The position sits in the LP Vault and stays in its pool. Its vault tokens are supplied to the Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy and are fully backed by that liquidity.
Vault tokens can be transferred only to approved Avana contracts, so LPVaultSwap is the only contract that can liquidate them.
After settlement
After a partial settlement, the borrower keeps the remaining position and its vault tokens, and the account's health factor is restored to the target.

After a full-position settlement, all vault tokens for the position are burned, and the NFT is released and settled through an approved route. Any surplus after debt, fees and costs is returned to the borrower.
Reverted liquidation

If any step fails, or the FirstLossReserve cannot cover a shortfall, the whole transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged. No deficit is recorded, and keepers may retry with a smaller partial liquidation.
Aave V4 records a deficit on the Avana Hub only when a completed standard Aave V4 liquidation uses up the collateral with debt remaining.
The sequence for liquidating an LP-backed position in a single transaction, from detection to flash-loan repayment.
Liquidation starts when an account's health factor falls below 1. Aave V4 handles eligibility and debt accounting. Avana's LPVaultSwap settles the LP collateral behind the vault tokens.

The whole liquidation runs in one transaction. A flash loan repays the debt and the vault tokens are burned. The matching liquidity is removed or the position is released. The proceeds are swapped to GHO and the flash loan is repaid.
Settlement modes, fees and shortfall handling are described in
Liquidation Framework
. This flow uses the vault-token pricing in
Price Oracles
Collateral Factors
Every liquidation either completes or reverts within one transaction, so there is no intermediate liquidating state. The outcome depends on the market's settlement mode.
Eligibility is based on LPOracle valuation, which uses Chainlink as the reference price and the pool's TWAP as a consistency check. Raw AMM spot prices do not reproduce these values.

How liquidation eligibility, flash-loan settlement and LP collateral removal are split between Aave V4 and Avana's contracts.

An account becomes eligible for liquidation when its health factor falls below 1. Aave V4 determines eligibility and handles debt accounting. Avana's LPVaultSwap contract uses a flash loan to repay the debt and settles the LP collateral backing it, all in one transaction.

Vault tokens can be transferred only to approved Avana contracts. LPVaultSwap is the only contract that performs liquidations. Each market has an approved settlement mode. Aave V4 layer

The Avana Borrow Spoke, a standard Aave V4 contract, tracks debt, vault-token collateral and the health factor. In partial-settlement markets it runs Aave V4's standard liquidation, including its target health factor and dust rules.
LPVaultSwap layer

LPVaultSwap takes the flash loan and triggers the liquidation or settlement. It burns the seized vault tokens and draws from the FirstLossReserve when needed. It then pays keepers, Avana and borrowers. LPVaultSwap is not a spoke and does not borrow from the Avana Hub.
LP Vault and settlement layer

The LP Vault removes the matching liquidity or releases the position for settlement. AMM settlement adapters redeem LP tokens and remove liquidity. They also collect fees and execute approved exits. Proceeds are converted to GHO through CoW Swap within the liquidation transaction.
Liquidation links Aave V4's accounting for vault-token collateral to the LP position held in the LP Vault. The rules below keep the two consistent.
Every vault token is backed
Vault tokens are minted 1:1 with deposited liquidity and burned on withdrawal or settlement. Every outstanding vault token is backed by liquidity in the LP Vault.
Seized vault tokens are burned
When vault tokens are seized or withdrawn for settlement, LPVaultSwap burns them and the LP Vault removes or releases the matching liquidity in the same transaction.
One transaction
The flash loan, debt repayment, liquidity removal, swap to GHO and flash-loan repayment all complete within the liquidation transaction. If any step fails, the transaction reverts.
Shortfalls are covered or the transaction reverts
If proceeds fall short, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged.

Each market has an approved settlement mode. Uniswap v2 LP tokens are fungible and can be redeemed in part. Partial settlement covers Uniswap v2 and selected Aerodrome or Uniswap v3 markets. In those Aerodrome and Uniswap v3 markets, liquidity can be partly removed while the NFT stays in the LP Vault.
Full-position settlement covers most AMMs that use NFTs. Adding any other AMM requires its own review and governance approval.
The steps depend on the market's settlement mode.
Partial settlement
• LPVaultSwap takes a GHO flash loan and calls Aave V4's standard liquidation, which applies the target health factor and dust rules.

• LPVaultSwap receives and burns the seized vault tokens. The LP Vault then removes the matching liquidity. For Uniswap v3, it removes part of the liquidity and the NFT stays in the vault. For Uniswap v2, it redeems the matching LP tokens. The proceeds are swapped to GHO and the flash loan is repaid.
• Normally, only the liquidity needed to restore health is removed, and the borrower keeps the rest. The dust rule may liquidate a small remainder in full.
Full-position settlement
• LPVaultSwap flash-borrows GHO and repays the debt through the Position Proxy's settlement authority.
• The Aave Adapter withdraws and burns all vault tokens for the position. The LP Vault then releases the NFT for settlement through an approved route.
• If the position is the account's only collateral, the full debt is repaid. Otherwise, repayment is sized to the approved health target.
• The surplus after debt, fees and costs is returned to the borrower. The Aave liquidation bonus does not apply in this mode.
Before liquidation, the position sits in the LP Vault and stays in its pool. Its vault tokens are fully backed by that liquidity.
Liquidation runs in a single transaction, so a position is never left partly settled. Either settlement completes, or the transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged.

After a partial settlement, the borrower keeps the remaining position and its vault tokens. After a full-position settlement, all vault tokens for the position are burned and any surplus goes to the borrower.

In partial-settlement markets, the Aave V4 liquidation bonus funds the keeper reward, execution costs and Avana's capped liquidation fee. Aave's built-in liquidation fee is set to 0 for vault-token reserves. The protocol fee is therefore charged once, in LPVaultSwap, as a fixed percentage of the bonus, and it does not add to the borrower's cost. In full-position markets, the keeper reward, costs and Avana fee are deducted from proceeds, up to a per-market maximum percentage of debt. The surplus goes to the borrower. Governance sets the bonus, fee and cap values for each market.

If proceeds fall short, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts, and keepers may retry with a smaller partial liquidation. Borrowing is activated only once a process for resolving such positions is in place. Aave V4 records a deficit on the Avana Hub only when a completed standard Aave V4 liquidation uses up the collateral with debt remaining.

strings: Welcome
What is Avana?
How It Works
Why LP Collateral Matters
Architecture
Pledge a supported LP position

A borrower pledges an approved Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity from the pool. The position keeps earning fees while it is in range.
Represent and value it

The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with the pledged liquidity. The AaveAdapter supplies them to the market's Avana Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy. The LPOracle values each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices, with no haircut. It then checks the result against the pool's TWAP.
Borrow GHO from the Avana Hub

Borrowing capacity is the position's value multiplied by the reserve's Collateral Factor. If capacity is sufficient, the borrower draws GHO from the Avana Hub. A capped GHO credit line from the Aave DAO funds the Hub.
Liquidity stays in the pool

Pledging an LP position moves custody to the LP Vault but leaves its liquidity in the underlying pool. The borrower can borrow GHO without first withdrawing the position and giving up its fees or range.
Valuation and limits are separate
The LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity with no haircut. Each reserve's Collateral Factor, min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor, sets how much of that value supports debt.
Liquidation has explicit rules

Each market has an approved settlement mode. LPVaultSwap uses a flash loan to repay debt and settle the LP collateral in one transaction. Partial settlement removes only the liquidity needed to restore health. Full-position settlement settles the whole position and returns any surplus to the borrower.
Introduction
Avana lets liquidity providers borrow GHO on Aave V4 against their Uniswap v2 and v3 positions. The positions stay active in their pools and keep earning trading fees.
Start with Key Concepts
Explore Borrow Spoke

Avana brings AMM liquidity positions to Aave V4 as collateral. A depositor pledges a Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. The depositor then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub while the position stays in the pool.
To borrow against LP assets elsewhere, a liquidity provider usually has to withdraw from the pool first. Withdrawing gives up trading fees and, for concentrated positions, the chosen range.

Avana keeps the position in its pool. The LP Vault holds the position, and a vault token represents it on an Avana Borrow Spoke. A vault token is a transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 record that maps 1:1 to the underlying liquidity. Avana runs on Ethereum mainnet with selected Uniswap v2 and v3 markets.

Each stage connects a user action to the protocol's accounting. A Pledge establishes custody. Valuation and the Collateral Factor determine borrowing capacity. A borrow creates GHO debt against that capacity. The following guides explain each step in detail.

LP collateral lets assets already deployed in an AMM support a GHO loan. The benefit is capital flexibility, not guaranteed positive carry. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk.

The Avana Hub and Avana Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. All Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts: LP Vault, AaveAdapter, LPOracle, RiskModule, CollateralizationModule, LPVaultSwap, AMMSettlementAdapters and AvanaConfig.

Each market category (Stable LP, Correlated LP and Blue-chip/stable LP) has its own Avana Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps. The Avana Hub holds the GHO credit line, and only approved Borrow Spokes can draw from it. A dedicated Position Proxy holds each borrower's Aave position. Deposits, borrows, repayments and withdrawals therefore pass through Avana's controls. The Avana Lend Spoke lets lenders supply assets directly to the Avana Hub. Aave governance approves it separately.

Avana does not fork, copy or modify Aave V4 code. The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. All Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts. The design follows the pattern of Babylon's native BTC integration on Aave V4.

Security review covers both contract execution and economic behavior. A valid contract call can still produce a wrong lending result if its price input is stale or its settlement route cannot execute. For this reason, oracle checks and in-transaction settlement are part of the design. Contract names may change after audits.
• LP positions are not ERC-20 reserves. Avana keeps custody in the LP Vault, separate from the vault tokens that represent positions on Aave. Every vault token must stay backed.

• Stale or manipulated prices can cause loss even when contracts execute as coded. LPOracle therefore uses Chainlink as the reference price, the pool TWAP as a consistency check, and maximum feed ages.
• Upgrades, pause and freeze roles, and configuration are privileged controls and part of the attack surface.

How first-loss capital, committed revenues and Avana Umbrella cover losses in Avana's Aave V4 markets.
Avana covers losses in three layers: dedicated first-loss capital, then revenues committed to loss coverage, then Avana Umbrella. Avana Umbrella is Avana's protocol safety module, named after
Aave Umbrella
. Collateral limits and liquidation remain the first controls against loss. Coverage is limited to the capital actually funded and committed. It is not a guarantee for every position.

If liquidation proceeds do not cover the debt being repaid, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged. Keepers may retry with a smaller partial liquidation. Borrowing is activated only once a process for resolving such positions is in place.

Aave V4 records a deficit on the Avana Hub only when a completed standard Aave V4 liquidation uses up an account's collateral with debt remaining. A liquidation that reverts does not create a deficit, and the debt stays on the account. The Avana Hub is a standard Aave V4 contract owned by the Aave DAO. Only approved Borrow Spokes have GHO draw capacity on it.

The first layer is dedicated first-loss capital held in the FirstLossReserve contract. Its size is set with Aave DAO service providers. The reserve counts toward coverage only once it is funded. A commitment alone is not coverage.
LPVaultSwap draws on the FirstLossReserve directly during liquidation, so first-loss capital is used before any deficit reaches the Avana Hub. Avana's monthly reports include first-loss resources.
Losses are absorbed in a fixed order. Each layer is used before the next.
1. Dedicated first-loss capital (FirstLossReserve) 2. Revenues committed to loss coverage 3. Avana Umbrella

The size of each layer, and which revenues are committed to loss coverage, are set with Aave DAO service providers and approved by governance. All interest revenue attributable to the GHO credit line accrues to the Aave DAO.

A shortfall found during liquidation is covered from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction, or the liquidation reverts. A deficit recorded on the Avana Hub after a completed standard liquidation is covered in the loss order above.

The Aave DAO's exposure is limited to the capped GHO credit line. Each increase to the credit line requires governance approval. Governance defines the exact settlement steps for covering a Hub deficit.

Avana Umbrella is the third layer of the loss order and is named after Aave's Umbrella. Its mechanics are not specified yet, including which assets can be staked, reward terms, slashing limits and withdrawal cooldowns. A separate governance approval sets them. Aave v3 Umbrella token addresses, cooldowns and parameters are not defaults for Avana.

The GHO credit line grows in stages. Each stage has its own conditions and requires governance approval. Only funded capital counts as protection, and amounts spent during liquidation are deducted from available coverage. Coverage applies to GHO deficits on the Avana Hub. Weekly usage reports and monthly revenue reports let readers check coverage against exposure. The reports include bad debt, FirstLossReserve usage, credit-line usage and first-loss resources. They also include successful, failed and retried liquidations.

Loss coverage applies to protocol shortfalls and deficits. It does not reimburse borrowers, who still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk. Coverage is limited to capital actually available. It does not increase borrowing capacity or remove liquidation risk. Risk Framework
How governance roles, the upgrade timelock and emergency controls apply to the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes and Avana's own contracts.

The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts: the LP Vault, AvanaConfig, Risk Module, Collateralization Module, LPOracle, AMM settlement adapters, Aave Adapter and LPVaultSwap.

Avana has three pool categories: stable, correlated and blue-chip/stable. Each category has its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps. Each market also has its own pool risk factor, settlement mode and oracle settings.

Three parties hold separate powers: the Aave DAO, Avana Labs and an Emergency Guardian multisig. Avana Labs submits and administers changes, and a designated risk reviewer reviews them. The Aave DAO approves changes and can stop markets. The Guardian can only pause, freeze and cancel.
Operating rule:
the Aave DAO can pause, freeze or stop Avana markets without Avana Labs, and Avana Labs cannot bypass the upgrade timelock.

Emergency powers can only stop or restrict activity. Borrowers can still repay and make permitted withdrawals by calling the contracts directly, without Avana's frontend.

Avana Labs owns, operates and pays for its own contracts, audits, monitoring and keepers. The Aave DAO's exposure is limited to the capped GHO credit line. Each increase to the credit line requires governance approval.
